title: Crisp Breaded Beef Cutlets with Lemon and Leaf Salad
summary: Thin beef cutlets pounded tender, coated in a cheesy herb crumb and fried until deep golden, served with a bright lemon-dressed leaf salad.
equipment: meat mallet or heavy pan for pounding
wire rack set on a baking tray, lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: thin beef sirloin or topside steaks, about 1 cm thick
fine sea salt or table salt
Parmesan-style hard cheese, finely grated (check the rennet)
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
small carrot, cut into fine matchsticks
small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.title: Flatten to even thickness
steps.text: Cut the beef into 4 equal pieces, then cover each one with cling film and flatten it with a mallet until it's an even 5-6mm thick. Pat the meat dry and season both sides with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Flattening breaks up the tougher muscle fibres so each cutlet cooks through quickly and stays tender rather than turning chewy.

steps.title: Set up three coating stations
steps.text: Put the flour in one shallow dish, beat the eggs in a second, and mix the panko, cheese, oregano, garlic and remaining 1/4 tsp salt in the third. Keeping each stage separate stops the coating turning gluey and helps every layer stick properly to the one before it.

steps.title: Coat the cutlets
steps.text: Dredge each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in the egg and let the extra drip away, then press it firmly into the crumb mixture on both sides. Lay the coated cutlets on the tray. The flour gives the egg something to grip, and the egg in turn acts as glue so the crumb layer stays put once it hits the hot oil.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour the oil into the frying pan to a depth of 4-5cm and heat it over medium-high until it reaches about 180°C, or until a stray breadcrumb sizzles the instant it touches the oil. Getting the oil to the right temperature first seals the crumb crust quickly, so it turns crisp instead of soaking up fat. Never leave hot oil unattended on the heat.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Fry two cutlets at a time for 2-3 minutes per side, until the crust is deep golden and crisp and the centre of the thickest cutlet reads at least 63°C on a thermometer. Let the oil come back up to temperature between batches so the next pair fries just as crisp as the first. Frying only a couple of cutlets at once keeps the oil hot, since a crowded pan cools it down and leaves the crust pale and soft.

steps.title: Drain and rest
steps.text: Lift the cutlets onto the paper-lined rack to drain while the next batch fries. Rest each cutlet for at least 3 minutes before serving, which gives the heat time to settle evenly through the meat.

steps.title: Toss the salad and serve
steps.text: Just before serving, toss the salad leaves, carrot and red onion with the lemon juice and oil. Serve the hot cutlets straight away with the salad and lemon wedges alongside. Dressing the salad at the last moment keeps the leaves crisp instead of wilting in the acid.

tips: Don't crowd the pan - frying more than two cutlets at once cools the oil and leaves the crumb coating soft and greasy instead of crisp.
Check doneness with a thermometer rather than guessing by time, since cutlet thickness can vary even after pounding.
Press the crumbs on firmly rather than just sprinkling them over, so the coating doesn't flake off in the oil.
Flatten the beef to an even thickness throughout, as thinner patches will overcook before the thicker parts are done.
Let the oil cool completely before you dispose of it, and never pour hot oil straight down the drain.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Cool any leftovers quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour, and use within 3 days. Reheat only once, until piping hot all the way through (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
